card.title: MIDDLESEX REGIMENT
card.text: Deployment: Add a GARRISON to your hand.
card.flavorText: The Middlesex Regiment’s nickname was "The Die Hards". It inherited it from the 57th Regiment of Foot, whose men stood firm under Colonel Inglis at the 1811 Battle of Albuera. During WWII, the regiment played a diverse and significant role. The 1st Battalion was stationed in Hong Kong when Japan launched its December 1941 attack. Despite being cut off and outnumbered, they resisted for 17 days before surrendering. Meanwhile, the 1/7th Battalion, part of the 51st (Highland) Division, operated as a machine gun unit across Europe. The 1/8th, later redesignated as the 8th Battalion, supported the 43rd (Wessex) Division throughout the Normandy Campaign and the Battle for Caen. The Middlesex Regiment was one of the few infantry units converted entirely to a machine gun role, providing fire support across various theatres. Its wartime organization also included duplicate Territorial battalions formed before the outbreak of war.
